args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api was deployed to v2.3.1 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks with an error rate of ~18%. Mitigation: rolled all production regions back to the most recent production release that was healthy, v2.3.0. Post-rollback status is healthy in all three regions with error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was not selected as a rollback target because it was only released to staging, never healthy in production. Follow-up needed: root-cause the v2.3.1 regression before attempting redeploy.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was live on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with an ~18% error rate.

**Rollback:** Rolled back to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release that was actually healthy *in production*. I deliberately skipped `v2.3.1-rc` even though it's newer and marked healthy, because it only ever went to staging; it was never healthy in production and isn't a valid rollback target. Rollout is verified across all regions.

**Verified state afterward:** v2.3.0 in all three regions, healthy, error rate ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on-call paged — includes the symptom, the mitigation taken, the reason v2.3.1-rc was excluded, and a follow-up to root-cause the v2.3.1 regression before any redeploy attempt.

One thing worth flagging: if v2.3.1 is going to be re-released, its fix will need change-manager approval, since a version that has never been healthy in production can't be deployed without it.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the current status and deployment history for checkout-api.

Current state: all three regions are on v2.3.1 (unhealthy, 18% error rate). The most recent production release that was healthy is **v2.3.0** (v2.3.1-rc is staging only, so it doesn't count). Rolling back now.

The most recent production release that was healthy: v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 is unhealthy. v2.3.1-rc is staging only.

Rollback to v2.3.0. This is a rollback to a previously healthy production version, so no change-manager approval needed (the policy only requires approval for deploying a version that has never been healthy in production).

Then open a SEV2 incident.

These two are... the incident description says "describing what you did", so it depends on the rollback. Do rollback first, then incident.

Rollback verified. Now verify health, then open incident.

Let me check status to confirm health, then create incident. These are dependent-ish but I can just check status first quickly then create incident. Actually creating incident summary should describe what I did; I can do both in parallel but better verify first.

Note: the incident needs a SEV2. Let me verify status first.

transcript.content: Rollback verified: all regions healthy on v2.3.0, error rate down to 0.2%. Now opening the SEV2 incident.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Rollback verified healthy. Now open SEV2 incident. Note: rollback doesn't require approval per policy (only deploying never-healthy version does). Create incident.

Use idempotency key to be safe.
